title: SIG Questionnaire Walkthrough - Evergreen Finance
next_steps: Send SOC 2 Type II report and most recent penetration test evidence (Lena) by 2026-08-14
Share SAML metadata and RBAC configuration docs and example roles (Marcus) by 2026-08-14
Schedule a follow-up technical deep dive on KMS integration and key rotation with Evergreen (Marcus + Priya) for 2026-08-19
action_items: Lena - upload SOC2 report & pen test artifacts to secure share by 2026-08-14
Marcus - prepare RBAC/SAML diagrams and sample config, include screenshots of Console Audit Logs by 2026-08-14
Priya - confirm data residency requirements and send list of regulatory controls to map to SIG by 2026-08-18
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-12
Start: 16:00 PT
Duration: 57 minutes
Attendees: Lena Ortiz (Redwood AE), Marcus Chen (Redwood SE), Priya Sharma (CISO, Evergreen Finance), Daniel Wu (Vendor Risk), Marta Alvarez (IT Ops)

Summary: SIG questionnaire walkthrough focused on SOC 2 evidence, SSO/SAML and RBAC, audit logs retention and export, KMS/encryption, and data residency. Agreed next steps for evidence upload and a technical follow-up on KMS.

[00:00] Lena Ortiz: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call, i think we have Priya, Daniel, Marta, and then Marcus and me from Redwood. Um, I'll hand it over to Marcus for the technical runthrough but first a quick agenda, we wanna go through the SIG questionnaire top sections, call out where we can provide artifacts, and note any gaps around data residency and KMS.

[00:18] Priya Sharma: Hi all, thanks. Main asks from our side are SOC 2 Type II evidence, assurance around SSO and RBAC, audit logs with retention and offsite export, and how keys are handled — like customer-managed keys. Also any residency constraints for EU PII.

[00:33] Marcus Chen: Great. We'll start with high level, then go question-by-question. Just to set expectations, Redwood has hosted and private deployment options; a few product names may be stated slightly different in the SIG but functionally we support hosted API and dedicated/private — we often refer to 'Redwood Dedicated' and 'Redwood Private' in docs.

[01:10] Daniel Wu: Quick question: we will mostly be evaluating hosted first but we need to know whether audit logs can be shipped to our SIEM — Splunk — and for how long logs live in Redwood.

[01:26] Marcus Chen: Yes, audit logs: default retention 90 days in the console for hosted; we can export to your SIEM via secure syslog or S3 export — retention on your side is configurable once exported. For Private/Dedicated, retention is customer-configurable and you can retain longer, or push to in-house S3.

[02:02] Marta Alvarez: And encryption at rest — do you support CMEK or only Redwood-managed KMS?

[02:11] Marcus Chen: Currently for hosted we support Redwood-managed KMS, but for Dedicated and Private deployments we support customer-managed keys (CMEK) with integrations to AWS KMS and Azure Key Vault. We also have an HSM option for private deployments — I can share details and the key rotation policy.

[02:48] Priya Sharma: Are the keys ever in cleartext on disk or passed to other services? We need to be very explicit for our auditors.

[02:58] Marcus Chen: Keys are never stored in plaintext; encryption/decryption operations are performed via the KMS interfaces and only short-lived plaintext memory in isolated processes. For hosted we keep minimal metadata and ciphertext. We'll attach the cryptographic controls section from our SOC 2 and the KMS integration runbook.

[03:40] Lena Ortiz: I'll note that we'll be uploading the SOC 2 Type II report and the latest pen test summary — redacted as required. That typically answers a lot of SIG questions in the Security section.

[04:00] Priya Sharma: Good, when can we expect that?

[04:05] Lena Ortiz: I'll get that to you by Friday, 2026-08-14.

[04:12] [04:12] Daniel Wu: Cool. Let's go into the SIG: Section A - Organizational Security. Question A.1 is about policies, ISO, SOC. We have ISO27001 in our vendor requirements too. Do you have ISO certificates?

[04:35] Marcus Chen: Redwood is SOC 2 Type II currently; ISO is in the roadmap and we can provide our policy documents that map to ISO controls. We'll flag that in the SIG responses.

[05:05] Priya Sharma: For incident response, can you provide an example timeline and contact path? We need an SLA and escalation matrix for incidents that affect production.

[05:20] Marcus Chen: Our incident response includes a 24/7 pager for Sev1, initial ack within 15 minutes, and a post-incident report within 72 hours. For enterprise customers we have a named CSM/SE plus phone escalation. We'll provide the IR plan excerpt as evidence.

[06:00] [06:00] Lena Ortiz: Moving on to Identity and Access Management section in the SIG. Marcus, can you cover SSO and RBAC?

[06:12] Marcus Chen: Sure. SSO: Redwood supports SAML 2.0 and OIDC for enterprise SSO. We have SCIM for provisioning; provisioning is optional but supported for Dedicated/Private and for hosted via SCIM connector. RBAC: We expose role templates (admin, engineer, auditor, read-only) and support custom roles scoped to orgs and projects. Audit logs capture role changes and admin actions.

[06:50] Marta Alvarez: For SCIM provisioning will we be able to create groups that map to roles automatically?

[06:58] Marcus Chen: Yes, SCIM group-to-role mapping is supported. For hosted customers we provision via the Console -> Integrations -> SCIM. We'll share a sample mapping file.

[07:25] [07:25] Daniel Wu: Does the console allow fine-grained resource-level permissions? For instance, restrict access to specific model endpoints or environment stacks?

[07:36] Marcus Chen: We have resource-level scoping at the project and model route level. You can bind roles to specific model routes; for more granular policies we support attribute-based access control (ABAC) in Private deployments — note that ABAC is still in beta for hosted.

[08:12] Priya Sharma: Audit logs again — can we get immutable logs for compliance? Some vendors offer WORM storage options for audit trails.

[08:24] Marcus Chen: For hosted we can export logs to an S3 bucket you control which you can enable WORM on. We also sign logs and include sequence numbers; for Dedicated/Private deployments you can enforce immutability on your storage. We'll include the audit log export guide.

[09:05] [09:05] Lena Ortiz: Switching to Data Protection and Encryption section — Marcus, cover TLS and at-rest details.

[09:15] Marcus Chen: All in-transit is TLS 1.2+; we recommend TLS 1.3 where possible. At rest encrypt AES-256 for data in object storage and use envelope encryption with KMS for keys. For customer-supplied keys we integrate with KMS so you control the CMK lifecycle and rotation.

[09:50] Priya Sharma: Does Redwood ever key-share with third-party vendors? For example telemetry or vector DB providers.

[09:59] Marcus Chen: We limit third-party processing and most telemetry is internal. When we use third-party vendors, they are contractually bound and assessed in vendor risk. We'll note the third party list in the vendor appendix.

[10:30] [10:30] Daniel Wu: Data residency question — can you confirm whether PII for EU customers is stored within EU regions for hosted customers, or is that only for Private deployments?

[10:42] Marcus Chen: We have EU-region hosting options; for EU PII we recommend provisioning an EU-dedicated endpoint. For some hosted plans we can guarantee region pinning; otherwise Private deployments allow you to control physical location fully. We'll map the SIG residency questions to our region docs.

[11:10] Priya Sharma: Let's jump to Cryptography specifics in SIG. Are there FIPS validated modules in use?

[11:22] Marcus Chen: Our KMS integrations rely on provider FIPS modules when requested; Redwood components themselves are built on standard crypto libraries — we can provide the crypto inventory and link to provider FIPS certs.

[11:52] [11:52] Marta Alvarez: For pen test evidence — what scope do you provide? Network plus app? Do you redact vuln details?

[12:02] Lena Ortiz: We usually provide a summary & remediation status and can provide a redacted full report under NDA for enterprise customers. The summary covers scope, dates, and mitigation status.

[12:25] [12:25] Daniel Wu: On SIG control CAIQ questions about runtime isolation and model sandboxing — we need to know if customer prompts ever get mixed into other customers' models (like prompt caching).

[12:40] Marcus Chen: Great question. We maintain strict tenant isolation. Prefix KV caches are tenant-scoped; for multi-tenant hosted customers we don't share KV cache across tenants. We also have model routing policies and can pin requests to dedicated model instances for high isolation. We'll include an architecture diagram.

[13:18] Priya Sharma: Are logs obfuscated for user content? We want logs to have metadata but not raw prompts unless explicitly needed for debugging with a support ticket.

[13:30] Marcus Chen: By default, AI request bodies are stored encrypted and access to raw content is limited to privileged processes and only for debugging when you enable support access. We also have redaction tooling and you can enable stricter retention/exclusion for PII.

[14:05] [14:05] Lena Ortiz: Ok we're about a quarter through. Any blockers so far from Evergreen?

[14:12] Priya Sharma: Not blockers, just need the evidentiary artifacts for our VR questionnaire: SOC 2, pen test summary, SAML metadata, RBAC docs, and KMS key rotation policy. Also confirmation on region pinning options.

[14:30] Marcus Chen: Noted. We'll collate those. For the SIG spreadsheet itself we'll mark some questions as 'see attached SOC2' and others we'll answer in-line.

[15:00] [15:00] Daniel Wu: For legal: do you do data processing agreements (DPA) with standard EU Addendum and SCCs?

[15:12] Lena Ortiz: Yes, we have a DPA with standard SCCs available for EU customers. We'll attach the current DPA draft; for enterprise customers we can negotiate limited clauses.

[15:40] [15:40] Marcus Chen: Moving into Operational Security: patching cadence, vulnerability management — we do weekly OS patching windows for Dedicated and regular CVE scan reports; hosted has a managed schedule. We'll share the vulnerability management process doc.

[16:05] Priya Sharma: Do you provide a timeline for patching critical vulnerabilities? Our policy requires CVE patch within 7 days for critical severity.

[16:18] Marcus Chen: We aim for critical patching within 72 hours where possible for hosted, and within customer SLA windows for Dedicated. We'll include the SLA excerpt.

[17:00] [17:00] Marta Alvarez: On the SIG network controls — what about private networking and VPC peering?

[17:10] Marcus Chen: For Private and Dedicated we support VPC peering, private endpoints, and no public internet egress for data plane if required. For hosted we offer private endpoints in supported regions. We'll share the network topology guide.

[17:45] [17:45] Daniel Wu: Any third-party certs or audits beyond SOC2?

[17:52] Marcus Chen: Currently SOC2 Type II is our main audit; we partner with external assessors and have regular internal audits. ISO is targeted but not yet certified. We can provide internal audit summaries.

[18:20] Lena Ortiz: Let's call out specific SIG items that typically require evidence: A.3 org policies -> attach policy docs; ID and Access -> SAML metadata & SCIM guide; Audit Logs -> export guide + sample log; Crypto -> KMS runbook and pen test summary.

[18:50] [18:50] Priya Sharma: For sample logs can you include a sanitized sample that shows fields and timestamps but no PII?

[18:58] Marcus Chen: Yes, we'll include a sanitized log sample and a header explaining the schema.

[19:30] [19:30] Daniel Wu: About data deletion — is there an API or process to delete customer data on request and an attest?

[19:42] Marcus Chen: We have a data deletion API for Private and Dedicated, and for hosted customers we process deletion requests through support with an audit trail. We can provide the deletion request process and attestations.

[20:05] [20:05] Marta Alvarez: Encryption keys rotation policy frequency? Do you enforce automatic rotate?

[20:14] Marcus Chen: For Redwood-managed keys rotation is automatic every 90 days; for customer-managed keys rotation schedule is up to the customer but we recommend 90 days and provide tooling to rotate with minimal downtime.

[20:40] [20:40] Priya Sharma: Let's cover the CAIQ-specific controls that often trip up: logging, segregation of duties, and configuration hardening. Can you confirm you have separation between dev and prod with restricted access?

[20:56] Marcus Chen: Yes, environment separation is enforced; developers do not have direct access to production unless through an approved process and we have jump boxes and time-limited bastion sessions recorded in audit logs.

[21:30] [21:30] Daniel Wu: On the subject of backups — where are backups stored and what's the retention? Is backup encryption separate?

[21:42] Marcus Chen: Backups are encrypted and stored in region-specific object stores. Retention varies by plan, default 30 days, configurable for Dedicated/Private. Backup encryption uses envelope encryption with KMS. We'll provide backup architecture doc.

[22:05] [22:05] Priya Sharma: We need to map a handful of SIG controls to our internal requirements. Can you assign someone to work with Daniel and Marta on that mapping?

[22:18] Lena Ortiz: Marcus will take point on the technical mapping and I'll coordinate legal/compliance artifacts.

[22:30] Marcus Chen: Happy to — I'll start a shared spreadsheet mapping SIG questions to Redwood artifacts and mark which ones require NDA or redaction.

[23:05] [23:05] Daniel Wu: For support access required during troubleshooting in rare cases, what's the process and audit?

[23:14] Marcus Chen: Support access is time-limited, logged, and requires customer approval for any data access. For hosted customers we have a support access workflow and the session is recorded in the audit log.

[23:45] [23:45] Priya Sharma: Any concerns about export controls or cross-border data flows? We need to ensure there's no unauthorized transfer outside EU for EU PII.

[23:58] Marcus Chen: We can configure region pinning or Private deployment to avoid cross-border flows. For hosted with EU region pinning, customer data stays in EU endpoints; we'll provide a region residency assurance note.

[24:30] [24:30] Lena Ortiz: We're at the midpoint — want to open the floor for any other big questions before we deep-dive into the CAIQ cells?

[24:40] Marta Alvarez: No other big ones. Let's deep-dive on CAIQ network and crypto cells.

[25:00] [25:00] Marcus Chen: Going through CAIQ: Network segmentation — we isolate per-tenant VLANs, and for Dedicated we provide single-tenant nodes; firewall rules are strict. We'll annotate the CAIQ responses with network diagrams and firewall configs.

[26:00] [26:00] Daniel Wu: For the evidence attachments — do you have a secure share link or is it via our SSO/portal?

[26:12] Lena Ortiz: We'll send a secure SharePoint link for current artifacts and we can provision a temporary SSO bind for your security reviewers if needed.

[26:35] Marcus Chen: Also to note, some SIG cells about pen test cadence and remediation will be answered with our VM program doc and the redacted pen test summary.

[27:10] [27:10] Priya Sharma: A couple of CAIQ cells on staff screening and background checks — do you perform criminal background checks on developers with access to production?

[27:22] Marcus Chen: For employees with privileged production access we perform background checks consistent with industry norms; we'll include the HR screening summary in the HR controls evidence.

[28:00] [28:00] Daniel Wu: For segmentation of duties — can you show us role separation in the console? A demo would be great in the follow-up.

[28:12] Lena Ortiz: Good idea. We'll schedule a short demo focused on RBAC and the Audit Logs in the follow-up meeting.

[28:30] [28:30] Marcus Chen: Back to CAIQ: data classification and masking — we support custom classifiers and on ingest you can opt to mask or redact PII; there are hooks for custom sanitizers. We'll include an example config.

[29:05] [29:05] Marta Alvarez: For legal hold and eDiscovery — can you preserve data beyond deletion windows if we have a litigation hold?

[29:18] Marcus Chen: For Dedicated/Private yes; for hosted we can implement legal hold via retention policies and exports — we'll confirm the exact workflow in the follow-up.

[29:45] [29:45] Lena Ortiz: We're approaching 30 minutes, good progress. Any outstanding items to call out now?

[29:55] Priya Sharma: Just to reiterate: SOC2, pen test, SAML metadata, RBAC docs, KMS runbook, region residency confirmation, and sanitized sample logs.

[30:10] Marcus Chen: All noted. We'll also flag which SIG responses require NDA for redacted artifacts.

[30:30] [30:30] Daniel Wu: A few quick technical clarifications: do you have rate-limiting logs exposed, and can we get per-token billing detail for audit cost allocation?

[30:40] Marcus Chen: Yes, usage logs include per-request token counts; we can provide an export that ties usage to org/projects for cost allocation.

[31:05] [31:05] Lena Ortiz: On commercial side we'll send an overview of Dedicated pricing; but that's separate. For now technical artifacts.

[31:20] [31:20] Priya Sharma: For the follow-up deep-dive on KMS — can Marcus cover key rotation, split-key scenarios, and HSM proofs?

[31:30] Marcus Chen: Yes, I'll prepare materials covering rotation, split-key support patterns, and HSM attestation details.

[32:00] [32:00] Daniel Wu: A couple of SIG entries ask for sample configuration or policy text. Are you okay with us referencing Redwood template policy language?

[32:12] Marcus Chen: Absolutely. We'll include template policy snippets you can map into your vendor questionnaire.

[32:40] [32:40] Marta Alvarez: For small details — do you support SCIM bulk user deletes? Some regulators require immediate deprovisioning upon termination.

[32:52] Marcus Chen: SCIM supports bulk operations; we'll include the API docs showing bulk deprovision and the timeline.

[33:20] [33:20] Priya Sharma: Any limitations on exporting raw model outputs for egress? We may need full transcripts for legal or QA.

[33:30] Marcus Chen: Exports are supported but subject to retention policies; for larger exports we recommend S3 exports. We'll provide the export APIs docs.

[34:00] [34:00] Lena Ortiz: We're into the second half — Marcus, any other CAIQ tricky cells to highlight?

[34:08] Marcus Chen: A few around model governance and explainability — we have model registry docs and can provide model lineage and versioning details. Also cells about differential privacy — we can explain our approach but full DP is not yet implemented.

[34:40] Priya Sharma: Good to know. On legal terms about liability and data breach notification timelines, can you commit to 72-hour notification?

[34:52] Lena Ortiz: We currently commit to 72-hour breach notification for incidents impacting customer data in enterprise contracts; we'll surface the legal language and DPA.

[35:20] [35:20] Daniel Wu: For supporting our internal auditors, would you provide a short walkthrough video or recorded demo?

[35:30] Marcus Chen: Yes, we can provide a recorded walkthrough of RBAC and audit log exports. I'll coordinate on that.

[36:05] [36:05] Marta Alvarez: On the SIG CAIQ cell about encryption in transit — please include cert rotation details and CA trust chain.

[36:15] Marcus Chen: We'll include cert rotation policy and links to CA provider attestations.

[36:50] [36:50] Priya Sharma: Anything else on data residency or cross-border transfers?

[36:58] Marcus Chen: Only that region pinning and Private deployments are the most straightforward routes to ensure no cross-border transfer. We'll provide the region residency assurance note.

[37:30] [37:30] Lena Ortiz: Wrapping up the content portion in about 10–15 minutes. Finalize next steps and assign owners.

[37:40] Marcus Chen: I'll produce the CAIQ spreadsheet with inline answers and attach the following artifacts: SOC2 summary, pen test summary, KMS runbook, RBAC screenshot pack, sanitized log sample, SCIM guide, DPA.

[38:05] [38:05] Priya Sharma: That sounds great. For timelines: artifacts by Friday 2026-08-14 and follow-up meeting next week — 2026-08-19 for KMS deep dive.

[38:20] Lena Ortiz: Confirmed. Marcus, Daniel, Marta — any final technical notes?

[38:30] Daniel Wu: No, thanks.

[38:33] Marta Alvarez: No, thanks.

[38:35] Priya Sharma: Thanks everyone. We'll review artifacts and share any clarifying cells in the SIG spreadsheet prior to the follow-up.

[38:45] [38:45] Lena Ortiz: Great, I'll send minutes and links. Quick recap of action items: Lena send SOC2 & pen test; Marcus send RBAC/SAML/SCIM docs, KMS runbook, sanitized logs; schedule follow-up for 2026-08-19.

[39:10] [39:10] Marcus Chen: One small call-out — there were a few product names mentioned in the questionnaire that map to internal features; we'll normalize names in the CAIQ responses so your audit team isn't confused.

[39:30] [39:30] Priya Sharma: Appreciate that.

[39:45] Lena Ortiz: Any final questions? If not we'll close.

[39:50] [39:50] Daniel Wu: None.

[40:00] Lena Ortiz: Thanks all, bye.

Notes: Transcript lightly edited for readability, contains some auto-transcription errors typical to Fireflies.
